passages.text: Introduction Our management’s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations (MD&A) is provided to assist readers in understanding our performance, as reflected in the results of our operations, our financial condition and our cash flows and should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and notes to consolidated financial statements included in Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data . The discussion in this MD&A contains forward-looking statements that involve substantial risks and uncertainties. Our objective is to also provide discussion of material events and uncertainties known to management that are reasonably likely to cause reported financial information not to be indicative of future results, which could differ materially from historical performance and from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements as a result of various factors such as those discussed in Item 1A. Risk Factors and Forward-looking statements and factors that may affect future results sections of this MD&A. A discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for fiscal 2025 compared to fiscal 2024 is presented below. A discussion regarding our financial condition and results of operations for fiscal 2024 compared to fiscal 2023 can be found under Item 7 of Part II of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, filed with the SEC on February 13, 2025 (our “2024 Annual Report”), which is available free of charge on the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov. Overview of our business We are a global leader in the animal health industry, focused on the discovery, development, manufacture and commercialization of medicines, vaccines, diagnostic products and services, biodevices, genetic tests and precision animal health. With a legacy of nearly 75 years, we continue to pioneer ways to predict, prevent, detect, and treat animal illness, supporting those raising and caring for animals worldwide - from veterinarians and pet owners to livestock producers. We manage our operations through two geographic operating segments: the United States (U.S.) and International. Within each of these operating segments, we offer diverse products for both companion animals and livestock customers in order to capitalize on local and regional trends and customer needs. credit_strengths.text: Zoetis is a global animal-health leader with roughly three hundred product lines sold across more than one hundred countries, spanning companion animal and livestock, which underpins revenue stability and pricing power through the cycle.
Operating margin sits well above the health care sector median and improved year over year, reflecting a high-value vaccine and diagnostics mix and disciplined cost control rather than one-off gains.

key_risks.text: Gross leverage rose year over year as debt increased while EBITDA grew only modestly, so the balance sheet absorbed new borrowings; leverage nonetheless remains below the sector median and inside the lower risk band.

Shareholder buybacks exceeded both operating cash flow and free cash flow, so distributions were funded partly from balance-sheet capacity; sustained repurchases at this pace would slow deleveraging and reduce refinancing headroom.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is strong and improved year over year, far above the sector median, leaving ample cushion against a moderate earnings decline; the debt stack carries no near-term maturity wall, with repayments beginning in the second year.

Free cash flow covers roughly a quarter of debt, below both the prior year and the sector median, while cash flow to debt also softened; coverage remains adequate but the trend warrants monitoring as borrowings rose.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is intermediate, with leverage comfortably below the next risk-band boundary and cash flow above its threshold; the weaker of the two measures drives the assessment, and headroom to downgrade is moderate.

Liquidity is a clear strength, with a current ratio well above one and above the sector median, and net leverage in line with peers; our judgement is that the issuer can absorb modest EBITDA pressure while funding research, capital spending and distributions.

credit_strengths.text: Zoetis 為全球動物保健領導者，擁有約三百條產品線，銷售遍及逾一百個國家，涵蓋伴侶動物與牲畜，支撐其於週期中的收入穩定性與定價能力。
營業利潤率遠高於醫療保健行業中位數，並按年改善，反映高價值疫苗與診斷產品組合及嚴格成本控制，而非一次性收益。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿按年上升，因債務增加而 EBITDA 僅溫和增長，資產負債表吸納了新借款；儘管如此，槓桿仍低於行業中位數，並處於較低風險區間之內。
股東回購超過經營現金流及自由現金流，故分派部分由資產負債表能力支持；若以此速度持續回購，將拖慢去槓桿進度並減少再融資空間。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率強勁並按年改善，遠高於行業中位數，對溫和盈利下滑留有充裕緩衝；債務結構並無近期到期牆，還款自第二年起開始。
自由現金流覆蓋約四分之一債務，低於上一年度及行業中位數，而現金流對債務比率亦轉弱；覆蓋仍屬充足，但隨著借款增加，趨勢值得監察。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為中等，槓桿舒適地低於下一風險區間邊界，而現金流高於其門檻；兩項指標中較弱者主導評估，下調評級的空間為中等。
流動性為明顯優勢，流動比率遠高於一且高於行業中位數，淨槓桿與同業相若；我們的判斷是發行人可吸納溫和 EBITDA 壓力，同時為研究、資本開支及分派提供資金。
